note: APUS-OpenJev-v1-4B revision 422b3741f8b5c092eeefef847c1ca89d78337d45, based on Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B. The full-depth released OpenJet decision API receives the official state and instructions with each full option text in the original order; ordinal score levels are represented as choices over every complete level description; binary guardrail items use APUS's native yes/no API. The exact upstream training-example overlap is unknown. This model was previously measured on the public 231-item split, so that split is exposed to model selection. Structured source-state objects were rendered as compact JSON for APUS’s text state field; source strings were preserved verbatim.
note_v14: Offline local open-weight inference on the frozen 308-item v1.4 set in a network-disabled, read-only container on an evaluator-owned Lium RTX PRO 6000 pod; no operator endpoint; no golds were exposed. Latency is the in-process APUS decision call on the serial standard+judge items with the self-hosted adjustment. Cost is estimated from the active hosted Qwen3.5-9B sibling price ($0.10/$0.15 per million input/output tokens) because DeepInfra marks the exact Qwen3.5-4B listing retired and replaced by 9B; APUS's measured prompt-token counts are used and generated output tokens are zero. This is a labeled proxy, not a GPU bill.
